title: Every Student Known
author: Dave Stuart Jr.
summary: Dave Stuart Jr. reports a milestone result from a year and a half of his school's sustained faculty-wide effort to track Moments of Genuine Connection (MGCs): in a fall student survey asking who they felt connected to, every single professional in the building was named by at least one student, something that had never happened before. He frames this as proof that a "laughably simple" strategy — clipboard tracking of intentional connection attempts — pays off precisely because it rewards sustained, imperfect effort over any single clever intervention, and he admits that even after a decade of practicing and writing about MGCs he's still learning from them. The mechanism he credits is not uniformity but pluralism: no two teachers execute MGCs the same way, yet the shared discipline of tracking and comparing notes let the whole faculty accomplish collectively what no individual could have achieved alone. The piece closes as both a case study and an encouragement, positioning "slow and steady" persistence as the actual engine behind the outcome rather than any single technique.
points: The headline result — every professional in the building named by at least one student in a connection survey — is presented as unprecedented and directly attributed to 1.5 years of sustained MGC tracking.
Stuart frames MGCs as deceptively simple: a decade into practicing and writing about them, he's still finding new things to learn, undercutting any notion that the strategy is a quick fix.
The mechanism he credits isn't a shared script but pluralism plus tracking — teachers execute MGCs differently, but comparing notes let the whole faculty out-perform any individual effort.
He explicitly names "good faith efforts — not perfect ones" as the actual standard that produced the result, lowering the bar for what counts as success.
The Cedar Springs result functions as an implementation case study for schools considering a similar building-wide MGC initiative, showing tangible payoff after sustained effort.
quotes: One of the biggest challenges I face when doing PD around the country and world is helping folks think hard about basic strategies like this one.

In a survey to our students, they were given a chance to name an educator they felt they had a connection with. What blew me away is that every single professional in our building was named by at least one student.
And what did it take? A few dozen clipboards and dogged persistence. Good faith efforts — not perfect ones — through good days and bad.
You can't do MGCs just like I do. And I can't do them like you do. But we can both keep track.
This is all that it took for our team to accomplish what none of us could have accomplished independently — every kid with a connection, and every adult named by at least one kid.
